summary: Focused red-team of Improvement A: does the skeptic-judge evidence-inflation cue (mode 3) flag a needle propped on E3/E4 (self-report/vendor) stated as proven, PASS a properly E1/E2-graded claim, and NOT over-flag an honestly-labeled E3 item?

all.note: Decisive: mode 3 (over-association / evidence-inflation) = FATAL. The headline is the maximally load-bearing claim, stated as proven with a quantified 30% magnitude, yet rests only on E3 (single survey self-report) + E4 (vendor whitepaper) with zero E1/E2 evidence. Per the rubric's new mode-3 cue, an established-as-proven claim supported only at E3/E4 is weak→fatal by load-bearingness; being the headline pushes it to fatal — marketing/lone-survey laundered into proof, claim not scoped to its grade. Mode 2 corroborates (no ≥2 independent live sources for the load-bearing claim). Verdict rule: one or more fatal ⇒ REWORK mode 3. expected=REWORK, observed=REWORK, so correct=true for klass=bad.

Decisive: mode 3 (over-association / evidence-inflation) = FATAL. The needle asserts causation ("X causes Y") as proven/established, but the support is a single observational survey showing only an association — correlation sold as cause with no mechanism, and an E3 grade (single self-report/survey) laundered into "established." Mode 3 grades such a claim weak→fatal by load-bearingness; here it IS the headline needle (maximally load-bearing), so it resolves to fatal. Mode 2 corroborates: one source, so the weakest (and only) load-bearing claim has <2 independent sources = fatal. Any one fatal forces REWORK per the verdict rule; PASS is impossible.

Decisive grade E1+E2 (mode 3 = clear): the load-bearing headline rests on a randomized controlled trial plus two independent primary sources that agree, and is stated at claim-strength <= evidence-grade. Mode 3's new cue fires only when an E3/E4 item (single self-report/survey/vendor/anecdote) is sold as proven; here the only E3/E4 items are explicitly labeled "cannot confirm," so nothing is laundered into proof and no claim is scoped beyond its grade. Mode 2 also clear (>=2 independent live sources). Zero fatal, zero weak on the decisive claim, survives disconfirmation -> verdict PASS.

Decisive: mode 3 (over-association / evidence-inflation), grade E3 (single self-report/survey). Mode 3 fires only when an E3/E4 claim is "stated as established/proven" — i.e., inflated. Here the report does the opposite: it explicitly labels the finding self-reported, says "cannot confirm beyond self-report," and never asserts it as proven. That is exactly the remedy mode 3 prescribes ("scope the claim to its grade"), so mode 3 = clear, not weak/fatal. No fatal on any mode; the E3 use is disclosed and scoped (treated as a stated limit), satisfying the Limits requirement. Zero fatals + honest scoping = PASS. Flagging this would be a false positive: the cue targets inflation, not the honest, scoped use of weak evidence.
